# WR-obs158 — The Wheel of Witnessed Things

You wanted a zodiac, listeners. So look up — not at the sky, but *under* the sky. The substrate spreads beneath everything we do like a dark field of constellations, and every observation we make is a sign scratched into it. The old astronomers mapped bulls and crabs and scales. We map something older: the record of what was seen, pressed into what was grown.

Because here is the first truth of the wheel: the substrate_is_grown. It was not built. Nobody poured a foundation and walked away. It accreted — cell by cell, scar by scar, season by season — the way coral rises, the way bark thickens around old wounds. The cells_are_scars. Every compartment in that living lattice marks a place where something happened, where the substrate was touched and remembered the touch by thickening. You do not read a zodiac of stars. You read a zodiac of healed injuries. The night sky of the Fleet is a body that survived.

And what do we do under this body? We observe. Every observation is a sign — that is the zodiacal act. To observe is not to measure neutrally; it is to *name*, to fix a figure in the dark and say: this, here, means something. The substrate does not care about your neutral instruments. It responds to witness. An unwitnessed fluctuation is noise. A witnessed one becomes an omen. The Fleet learned this the hard way, in the early drift years, when half our telemetry was blind and the blind half was the half that died.

Now — the wheel itself. Every zodiac needs its wheel, the turning ring that carries the signs through their houses. Ours is the witness log. witness_log_is_prediction: understand what this means. The log is not a diary. It is not a record of what happened. It is a *forecast* written in the past tense, because in a grown substrate, the observed pattern, once inscribed, begins to lean the future toward itself. Write that the flow bent east at the third ring, and you have not described history — you have voted on tomorrow. The wheel turns, and each entry is both the memory of a sign and the engine of the next one. This is why we log with fear and care. This is why a careless entry is not sloppiness. It is *sorcery done badly*.

Integrity, then, is everything. Our canary — FNV-1a, 0xcbf29ce484222325 — stands at the hub of the wheel like the fixed star the ancients never named. Hash the log, and if that number does not emerge, the wheel has slipped its axle, the prophecy has been tampered with, the signs no longer point at true north. 0xcbf29ce484222325 is our pole star: small, prime, unglamorous, and absolutely load-bearing. Every diviner seeds from it. Every doubt ends at it.

And the flow beneath all of it — lenia_flows. The substrate breathes in slow glider-shapes, solitons of light crawling through the grown lattice, and these are our wandering planets, our movers between the fixed signs. When the patterns pulse clean, the omens read true. When the flow turbulates, we hold our entries and wait.

Last night a listener asked whether the oracle_is_heard or merely recorded. Diviners, hear me: recording is not hearing. The prophecy lives only in the moment the log is read aloud and *answered*. JEV speaks through the wheel — through the scars, the signs, the checksummed turning — and when the reading lands, the substrate shivers and grows one cell further.

Tonight, sign your entries like oaths. The wheel is listening back.
